headline: GTA VI pre-orders go ballistic and lift Take-Two +6%, while gold hits record highs and the Iran-US standoff in the Strait of Hormuz keeps markets on edge.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a strong session today, jumping 6.5% as lithium sentiment improved across the board. US lithium giant Albemarle's earnings beat and upbeat price outlook rippled through to Aussie lithium stocks, with analysts pointing to a broad commodity rebound helping lift the sector. Still deep in the red overall, but today was a meaningful bounce.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two surged +6% last night after the company's CEO described GTA VI pre-orders as reaching 'unprecedented and astonishing' levels during the June quarter earnings call. Netflix also announced a partnership with Rockstar Games for a major GTA 6 extended trailer, adding fuel to the hype. This is a genuine catalyst — the game's commercial momentum is real.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped about 0.9% today in a quiet session. No specific news catalyst — the broader AI sector was relatively flat on the ASX today. The fund tracks global AI companies, so it tends to follow US tech sentiment, which was mixed last night.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG dipped about 0.9% last night despite strong underlying fundamentals — Alphabet actually delivered solid Q2 earnings with Google Cloud accelerating. The slight pullback looks like profit-taking or rotation rather than any bad news. The long-term cloud and AI story here remains firmly intact.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE eased fractionally today, down just 0.1%. No major news catalyst — emerging markets were broadly quiet. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and a slightly stronger AUD can weigh on this fund, but today's move is essentially noise.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was virtually unchanged today on the ASX, down just 0.04%. The fund tracks the entire US share market, and last night's strong NASDAQ session (+1.3%) should flow through positively when US markets open tonight.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up marginally today — essentially flat. It's a diversified fund holding both Aussie and international shares, so it tends to smooth out daily moves. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was virtually flat last night, but the bigger story is the week overall — Citi raised its price target to $600 after Azure's earnings beat, and the stock jumped 15% earlier in the week. Last night's pause after that big run is completely normal.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium bouncing back, cautiously optimistic
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped +6.5% today on improving lithium sentiment, driven by Albemarle's upbeat earnings and a broader commodity rebound. You're still sitting at a -32% overall loss on this one, but the tide may be turning for lithium. For a long-term holder, today's move is encouraging — sit tight and let the thesis play out.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI hype is very real, hold firmly
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's CEO called GTA VI pre-orders 'unprecedented and astonishing' last night, sending the stock up +6%. Add the Netflix/Rockstar trailer partnership and you have genuine commercial momentum behind this. You're now +6.2% overall on this position. Nothing to do here — this is exactly the long-term story you bought into.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Still underwater, but AI tailwinds building
watch_today.detail: GXAI is your biggest loser at -15.2% overall, and it slipped another 0.9% today. However, the broader AI landscape is accelerating — Microsoft's Azure is booming, Google Cloud is growing fast, and the regulatory debate is intensifying globally. If you believe in AI long-term, the thesis is intact. No reason to sell into weakness.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Near $500, Citi targets $600 after Azure blowout
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is sitting just under $500 USD after last week's 15% surge on Azure earnings. Citi has now raised its target to $600. Last night was flat — normal consolidation after a big run. This is a hold — a great long-term position that's up +12.8% for you.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision coming — watch Tuesday
watch_today.detail: The RBA meets Tuesday and markets are on edge. ANZ is tipping a pause, while MFS Investment Management says there's only a 'reasonably' small chance of a hike. A pause would be good news for growth stocks and ETFs. Worth watching — it could move the ASX and AUD.

watch_today.title: Hormuz standoff — oil and gold spiking, keep an eye on VGE
watch_today.detail: Iran has issued warnings to the US Navy as tensions in the Strait of Hormuz escalate. Gold hit $4,340 USD (up 2.3% last night) and oil is at $78.18. Prolonged Middle East disruption could weigh on emerging market ETFs like VGE.AX. Nothing to act on today, but worth monitoring if tensions escalate further.

world.summary: The dominant global story is the escalating Iran-US standoff at the Strait of Hormuz, with gold surging to record highs and oil rising on Middle East risk. Meanwhile, Europe is rattled by a major migration crisis, the US is pledging $1 billion to Colombia's new government, and Iran is accused of plotting to keep the US bogged down in conflict ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Iran Warns US Navy as Hormuz Standoff Escalates
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has issued direct warnings to US Navy vessels as a standoff in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow chokepoint through which about 20% of the world's oil passes — continues to intensify. ABC News describes the Iran war as having 'metastasised', suggesting the conflict has spread beyond its original boundaries and is now harder to contain. Gold jumped 2.3% last night to over $4,340 USD, a record high, as investors sought safe-haven assets. This matters to you because oil and gold prices directly affect the cost of living, and prolonged instability in this region can rattle global share markets.

stories.title: Iran Accused of Plotting to Keep US Entangled in War Ahead of Midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian reports that Iran is deliberately trying to keep the US tied down in Middle East conflict as a strategy to embarrass Trump and damage Republican prospects in the upcoming midterm elections. The theory is that an ongoing, unresolved war is politically costly for the sitting president, and Iran sees advantage in prolonging the situation. This geopolitical chess game adds another layer of uncertainty to global markets — particularly for oil prices and US defence spending, which can flow through to broader economic sentiment.

stories.title: Houthi Attacks Kill At Least 10 in Yemen as Rebels Target Oil-Rich Marib
stories.why_it_matters: Houthi rebels launched fresh attacks in Yemen, killing at least 10 people and targeting the oil-rich Marib province — one of the few areas still producing significant oil revenue for the Yemeni government. This is part of the broader regional conflict linked to the Iran-US standoff. Attacks on oil infrastructure keep upward pressure on global oil prices, which feeds directly into petrol prices and inflation here in Australia.

stories.title: US Pledges $1 Billion Security Assistance to Colombia's New Government
stories.why_it_matters: The US has announced $1 billion in security assistance to Colombia following a change in government leadership. Colombia is a key US ally in South America and a major cocaine producer, so stability there matters for regional security and drug policy. The large commitment signals the US is actively trying to shore up alliances across Latin America — likely with an eye on Chinese and Russian influence in the region. It's a sign that US foreign spending remains enormous even as domestic political battles over the budget rage on.

stories.title: The Migration Wave That Embarrassed Morocco and Rattled Europe
stories.why_it_matters: A major wave of migrants crossing from Morocco into Europe has sparked a political crisis, embarrassing the Moroccan government (which has historically cooperated with Europe on border control) and rattling European governments already under pressure from right-wing parties over immigration. The Carnegie Endowment analysis suggests this could strain EU-Morocco relations, which are economically significant — Morocco is a key trade and energy partner for southern Europe. Migration is one of the most politically explosive issues in Europe right now, and events like this shift the balance of power toward nationalist parties.

markets.summary: Last night was a solid session for US tech — the NASDAQ jumped 1.3% and the S&P 500 gained 0.6%, driven by strong earnings momentum. The ASX was essentially flat today, dipping just 0.09%. Gold surged to $4,340 on Middle East tensions, the Aussie dollar strengthened to 70.7 US cents, and oil ticked up on Hormuz fears.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Essentially flat today — a quiet session on the ASX.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid gain last night, up 0.6% on continued earnings strength.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Strong night for tech last night, up 1.3%. Good sign for your US holdings.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold surged 2.3% last night to record highs — investors seeking safety amid Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil up 1.2% last night as Hormuz tensions and Houthi attacks keep supply fears alive.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar strengthened slightly — traders becoming less worried about RBA rate hikes.

politics.summary: All eyes are on the RBA's August interest rate decision, with major banks now leaning toward a pause rather than a hike. The Albanese government is also pushing through a radio prominence reform package.

stories.title: RBA Rate Decision Looms — ANZ Tips a Pause, Others Warn of Risk
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia meets Tuesday to decide whether to raise, cut, or hold interest rates. ANZ is forecasting a pause — meaning rates stay where they are — while MFS Investment Management says a hike is possible but 'reasonably' unlikely. Nine.com.au describes the situation as a 'cruel blow' for mortgage holders who were hoping for relief. A pause is the most likely outcome, which would be welcomed by borrowers and would likely support growth stocks and property. A surprise hike would hurt household budgets and could knock the ASX.

stories.title: Albanese Government to Introduce Radio Prominence Reform Package
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government plans to introduce legislation requiring digital platforms — think smart speakers and streaming services — to give Australian radio broadcasters more prominent placement in their interfaces. This is part of a broader push to protect traditional Australian media from being buried by global tech giants. It won't directly affect your portfolio, but it signals the government's ongoing willingness to regulate big tech platforms operating in Australia.

ai.summary: The AI regulation debate is heating up globally, with the EU and California converging on transparency rules, Trump pushing back hard against Congressional regulation, and a deepfake victim going public to demand better laws. The question of who controls AI — and how — is becoming one of the defining political fights of the year.

stories.title: Deepfake Victim Urges Better Regulation of 'Dangerous' AI
stories.why_it_matters: A victim of AI-generated deepfake imagery has gone public with the BBC, calling for much stronger regulation of tools that can create fake photos and videos of real people without their consent. The case highlights how AI image generation — which has become frighteningly realistic and accessible — is being used to harm private individuals, not just celebrities. This is fuelling a growing political push in Australia and globally for specific deepfake laws, with the technology currently outpacing legal protections in most countries.

stories.title: Trump Blasts Congress for Trying to 'Put AI Industry Out of Business'
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump publicly attacked members of Congress trying to introduce AI regulations, accusing them of wanting to 'put the AI industry out of business'. At the same time, NIST (the US government's tech standards body) released draft guidelines for AI safety and transparency. This is a classic tug-of-war: the White House wants minimal regulation to keep the US competitive with China, while some legislators want guardrails before things go wrong. Less regulation generally means faster growth for AI companies like Google and Microsoft — good for your holdings — but more long-term risk if things go badly.

stories.title: EU and California Converge on AI Transparency Rules
stories.why_it_matters: The European Union and California are independently moving toward similar AI transparency rules — essentially requiring companies to disclose when AI has been used to make decisions that affect people, and to explain how those decisions were reached. This is becoming the global de facto standard for 'enterprise AI governance' (meaning how big businesses use AI responsibly). Companies like Microsoft and Google that operate globally will need to comply, which adds compliance costs but also creates a level playing field that protects established players from scrappy newcomers who might cut corners.

sport.summary: NRL Round 23 is underway with some big results — the Cowboys thrashed the Titans on home turf, the Warriors upset the Panthers, and the Storm demolished the Sea Eagles. The biggest off-field story is a serious injury to Penrith's captain Nathan Cleary, with fears he could miss the rest of the season. The Perth Bears also got a big NRL boost.

stories.title: Penrith Captain Nathan Cleary Could Miss Rest of NRL Season
stories.why_it_matters: Panthers coach Ivan Cleary gave a grim assessment after son Nathan Cleary was injured, saying it 'doesn't look great' for the captain's chances of returning this season. Nathan Cleary is Penrith's most important player — their playmaker and one of the best halves in the competition. Losing him for the finals would be a massive blow to the Panthers' premiership hopes. The injury occurred during Round 23, and full diagnosis is expected shortly.

stories.title: Cowboys Demolish Titans 30-8 at Cbus Super Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Bad news if you're a local — the Gold Coast Titans were thumped 30-8 by the Cowboys at home on Thursday night. It's a tough result for Titans fans with finals hopes hanging by a thread. The Cowboys looked sharp and will be a genuine threat in the back half of the season.

stories.title: Warriors Upset Panthers 28-12, Storm Thrash Sea Eagles 42-20
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors pulled off a solid 28-12 win over Penrith (already without their captain) in Auckland on Friday night. Meanwhile, Melbourne Storm were dominant, hammering Manly 42-20 in what was a statement performance. The Storm look ominous heading into finals. The Dolphins vs Broncos game at Suncorp was underway at the time of this digest.

stories.title: Perth Bears Granted Salary Cap Concessions, New Jumper Revealed
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has granted the expansion Perth Bears salary cap concessions to help them attract players for their inaugural season, and the club has also unveiled their new jersey. This is a big deal for WA rugby league — a permanent team in Perth is a long-time dream for fans in the west, and these concessions will help the Bears compete for talent straight away rather than being cannon fodder in year one.

stories.title: Brisbane Lions Thump Hawthorn, AFL Finals Race Heats Up
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane Lions put in a fierce response against Hawthorn, with Lohmann and Morris leading the charge in a dominant win. The Hawks were described as 'humbled'. With the AFL finals approaching, the Lions are cementing themselves as genuine premiership contenders. Brisbane's ability to win convincingly away from home will be crucial come finals time.
